thread:
erica: Quick async standup — SLO/alerting/oncall follow-ups

What I did:
- Finished the canary for the new routing fallback (deployed v1 -> v1b). Metrics collected for last 2h.
- Toned down a noisy alert rule (5xx spike detector) to reduce paging during GC thrash.

Blockers / notes:
- Canary traffic showed a small tail-latency bump around 95th pctl when batch size > 16. Need a quick perf profile.
- Runbook clarity: the rollback steps for route-fallback aren't obvious to oncall. Suggest adding a one-liner.

Today / asks:
- @mike can you take a quick look at the canary perf traces? pinged you for CR.
- @chen can you add a short rollback snippet to the runbook (how to pin traffic back to primary model)?
- I'll open a short alert tweak PR for debounce and escalation windows.

mike: Ack — I'll pull traces now. If it's batching-related we can try reducing max_batch and re-measure.

chen: On it. I can add a single `kubectl` pin example and a note about TTL for the route. Will push an edit in ~30m.

sam: Saw the same tail-latency in synthetic runs yesterday. I ran `curl` against the canary endpoint, reproduced a few 95th spikes when sequences were long.

sam: Command I used:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood-canary.example/generate -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":512}' | jq '.latency'
```
erica: Nice, thanks. If it's reproducible with the `curl` test that's helpful. Could be an attention-kernel path on those GPUs.

dev-bot: [deploy] canary routing v1b -> active (10% traffic) — success :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Alert: `SLO_latency_95_pctl` crossed warning threshold for service:inference-canary at 3832105001 — paging suppressed (debounce active)

mike: I see logs with longer KV cache sync times when batches are larger. Pasted snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T15:12:03Z WARN kv_cache: sync took=123ms entries=512
2026-03-17T15:12:05Z INFO batcher: dispatch size=24 latency=142ms
```

mike: Hypothesis: larger batches trigger a different code path that does extra KV syncs. I'll instrument and run a targeted 1-1 test with batch_size cap=16.

chen: Runbook edit PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runbooks/pull/987 — added `kubectl rollout undo` example and a note about traffic-pin TTL. Please review.

erica: Reviewed, lgtm. Small nit on wording but fine for oncall.

sam: If mike wants, I can run the reduced-batch synthetic ramp and post the graphs to the #dune dashboard.

mike: That would be great. If latency smooths out with cap=16 we can temporarily lower max_batch in the deployment and watch SLOs.

erica: I'll open the alert PR to extend debounce from 30s -> 90s and add a second-tier severity for sustained crossings. Will link here once created.

sam: FYI I also tagged @ops-rotation for visibility — they might want to skip noisy pages while we tune. :slightly_smiling_face:

oncall-bot: Note: nightly scheduled maintenance window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC — any deploys that require rollback should be coordinated.

erica: Thanks all. Next steps: mike runs instrumented perf test, sam posts Dune graphs, chen merges runbook PR, I open alert tweak PR. If anyone hits an urgent page call out in channel and we'll escalate.

mike: starting tests now, will update in ~20m.

chen: PR merged.

sam: Dune link: https://dune.internal/redwood/graphs/canary-latency (posting screenshots in thread)

mike: quick update — reduced batch cap to 16 in a canary patch, preliminary 95th pctl down ~18ms. continuing run for 10m.

erica: solid. If that holds we can ship a temporary hotfix to prod then schedule a proper kernel/path fix.

someone_else: +1 for hotfix, and please add a short rollback checklist line to the incident page too.

erica: Will do — adding to incident page now. Thanks everyone. :team-rocket:
